tail:
Done. Both artifacts written; `scaffold-verdicts` accepts all three of my rows (the four remaining `verdict-missing` errors are group a's pages, batches 6–8).

**Verdicts — all three pairs `insufficient`, none of them for thinness.**

| pair | blocking finding |
|---|---|
| `lagrange-four-square-theorem` | **B1-1** — `lem-four-square-congruence-for-primes` re-derives the published `prop-every-nonzero-residue-mod-prime-is-a-sum-of-two-squares` step for step, from the identical five dependencies. The Beta declined to cite it because `sums-of-two-squares` was `status: draft` at 03:31 and pre-authorised the switch "if frontier-17's pair is published before step 5". It reads `published` on disk now. Until it lands, the A page has zero `deps` edges to its sole declared prerequisite. |
| `finite-fields-and-cyclotomic-extensions` | **B3-1** — five items plan `provenance.statement: ai-generated` on a `remark` and four `false-statement`s; `content-policy`'s `GENERATED_ROLE` covers only `corollary`/`example`/`counterexample`, so each is a hard `generated-kind` error at step 5. No run has shipped one since 2026-08-01. **B3-2** — `ex-the-subfield-lattice-of-the-field-of-order-two-to-the-twelve` declares that remark in its `deps`, contradicting the notes' own twice-stated load-bearing check. **B3-3** — Wedderburn's decline is right but its reason is false (the class equation *is* published, at order 42) and its destination is a published page. |
| `noetherian-rings-and-hilbert-basis` | **B4-1** — Hochster Cor. 5.9 deferred on the premise that `cor-principal-ideal-domains-are-noetherian` is unpublished; it is published, in closure, and the reason conflates it with a different statement. One-line corollary, dead-end destination. |

I adjudicated all 30 Beta findings (9 + 11 + 12) individually. Two Alpha decisions the Betas handed up: **declined** Hochster Thm 5.5 as a second Hilbert-basis proof (it proves a *weaker* statement than the page already proves, and needs a lemma `noether-normalisation-and-nullstellensatz` owns); **recorded for the owner** Conrad Thm 5.1, a genuinely different route to the published two-square theorem, blocked only because the reciprocal cross-reference needs an edit to a published page.

I made no scaffold edits and no `plan-spec.json` edits — both drift edges were already applied, and each fix has to move `pages.json`, `proof-contracts.json` and the notes together, which is the Beta's hand at `3-fix`.

Gates run over batches 1/3/4: `coverage-checklist` 380 results 0 errors; `url-sweep --recover --fail-on-dead` 14/14 live; `validate-plan` OK; 419 external dependency uses over 168 published items, **0** outside closure, **0** forward-order, **0** b-leaf violations, **0** with an `ai-generated` statement. I also verified both Euler sign patterns and Hamilton's as genuine identities over 200k random quadruple pairs, and recomputed every worked number on batch 1's B page.

One thing for you: **`validate-plan.mjs` does no reading-order check on a dependency that already exists in `items/`** — the main loop's `if (existing.has(d)) continue;` makes the order comparison unreachable, and the b-leaf rule was patched around it in a separate loop but the order test never was. A new page can cite a published item homed *later* in reading order and the gate passes. Batch 4 nearly hit it with formal power series at order 193. I checked my six pages by hand (clean); groups a, b and d should be asked, because the gate won't say.
